A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Backward Conformal Prediction, with matching main sections and Appendices A–C; v2 adds Appendix D. Text, equations, figures and appendices are available and readable.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B report original CIFAR-10 and Breast Cancer Wisconsin experiments, including accuracy, coverage distributions and prediction-set counts.

after.justification: V2 retains the original classification experiments and their reported accuracy, coverage and prediction-set outcomes.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds an auxiliary estimator averaging squared leave-one-out pseudo-miscoverages for its alternative coverage bound. Algorithm 1, the e-value construction, prediction-set selection and original mean leave-one-out estimator remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CIFAR-10 multiclass and Breast Cancer Wisconsin binary classification tasks, retaining fixed and adaptive size-constraint scenarios. Neither adds regression experiments.

E2.justification: Appendix B.2 retains the same standard conformal prediction comparisons at alpha = 0.02 and alpha equal to mean adaptive miscoverage. The top-T alternative discussed in v2's Remark 3.4 is not newly evaluated.

E3.justification: Training settings, data splits, calibration sizes, size constraints and testing procedures are unchanged. Both retain n = 100, 1000 and 5000, binary-search tolerance 0.005, and the adaptive rule's k = 20.

E4.justification: The calibration-size and set-size analyses, individual-run histograms, and local-entropy adaptive-size illustration are retained unchanged in Figure 3 and Appendix B. No new empirical ablation, robustness test or diagnostic analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both versions report N = 200 repetitions with the same histograms and mean/coverage indicators. No experimental seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests are added; Appendix D's probability bounds concern method theory.

E6.justification: The empirical figures and numerical outcomes are unchanged, including CIFAR-10 training/test accuracies of 98.6%/91.1%, breast-cancer test accuracy of 97.7%, and standard-conformal set counts of 1/166/33 and 196/4 in Appendix B.2.

T1.justification: New Appendix D introduces Theorem D.1, Corollary D.2 and a proof using Cauchy–Schwarz and second-moment estimation to derive an alternative to the Taylor-based coverage argument. It adds moment and sample-size assumptions. Existing Section 3 and Appendix C results are retained; Theorem 3.4 becomes 3.5.

C1.justification: The introduction newly claims a calibration-estimable coverage guarantee without Taylor approximation, referring to Appendix D. The abstract and principal contributions concerning size control and leave-one-out estimation remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Remark 3.4 newly explains that direct empirical top-T miscoverage estimation suffices for constant size under i.i.d. sampling, distinguishing the harder data-dependent case. The conclusion adds discussion of conservatism from Markov's inequality and the size–coverage tradeoff.

D1.justification: V2 removes Section 4's statement and GitHub link providing access to code and experimental setup, without a replacement. The reported implementation parameters, hardware and runtime information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 now attributes the e-variable construction to Wang and Ramdas (2022) and newly cited Koning (2025), identifying Balinsky and Balinsky (2024) as its conformal application. Appendix A is substantively unchanged; publication updates for existing references do not add works.

P1.justification: Most prose and the existing section order are retained. Local revisions add Appendix D references, an explanatory remark and a conclusion paragraph, alongside changes to attribution, author presentation and acknowledgments.

P2.justification: V2 reformats the document throughout using the NeurIPS template, changing page geometry, typography, margins, title/author layout and figure scaling and placement. Figure 1 moves from page 2 to 3, for example. All ten figures retain their original graphical content.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful clarification and a potentially important alternative to v1's Taylor-based guarantee. However, Theorem D.1's n > min(...) condition does not enforce all thresholds its proof uses, and page 27 takes expectations of a high-probability inequality without accounting for the exceptional event. These unresolved theoretical issues, together with removal of the code-access link, prevent a reliable net-improvement judgment.
